standalone.observation: The anecdote (flyers, doors, bench, repair) reads fine alone, but the recurring Capitalized-Term-plus-definition pattern feels like a glossary insert rather than performed speech to someone outside the deck format.

performer.observation: Dry, self-deprecating humor carries a clear voice, e.g. "Last time it was me and a thermos, so this is a movement."

storyBetweenCards.observation: A full week unfolds in order: flyers, doors, Saturday repair, the following week's hinge, Sunday write-up, a pilot stripe, then a cost reckoning and sign-off.

individuality.observation: Concrete props (staple gun, loose slat, terrible hat) give texture, but the doubt-to-small-win-to-compounding arc is a familiar community-organizing shape.

outro.observation: Rejecting the applause and naming "the Core Question" lands as a sharp turn, but "Stay Fluffy, Folks!" closes on an unrelated jingle-like tag.

transferable.observation: The engine is a narrator's organizing story interrupted by named, defined concepts; swapping the concept names and surface props could reskin this for another topic with little else changed.

flags.observation: "the future is a process of slow, incremental improvement you participate in" closely echoes the synopsis wording, reading as a mission statement rather than observed detail.
"Your nervous system thinks that is death" introduces clinical/therapy register amid otherwise concrete door-to-door narration, a sudden tonal jump.
"the feed" names no specific platform or prior reference; the line floats as general media commentary disconnected from the bench scene around it.
"a stuck system" has no established referent in the surrounding text; it is abstract against the concrete objects (slat, bench, hinge) nearby.
"subscriptions" and "tickets" draw on two different media economies (streaming/newsletter vs. cinema box office) inside one couplet.
"Stay Fluffy, Folks!" shifts tone sharply from the reflective closing lines; "fluffy" has no earlier reference anywhere in the piece.
